did_you_know.text: Did you know? Pashhur son of Immer is described as a priest and as “chief officer in the house of the LORD”—a senior official in the Temple—and he heard Jeremiah’s prophecy.
Did you know? After hearing Jeremiah’s words, Pashhur had him beaten and put in the stocks at the Upper Benjamin Gate, within the Temple grounds.

Did you know? The next day, Pashhur released Jeremiah, but Jeremiah told him that the LORD would no longer call him Pashhur, but “Terror on Every Side”—a name expressing fear and dread from all directions.
Did you know? Jeremiah prophesied that all the treasures of Judah’s kings, the city’s wealth, and the fruits of its labor would be handed over to Judah’s enemies and taken to Babylon.
Did you know? The punishment pronounced on Pashhur included exile and death in Babylon, and he and all his friends would suffer because he had prophesied lies to them.
Did you know? Jeremiah describes his calling as a struggle: he felt enticed to speak, overpowered, and mocked all day long.
Did you know? Although Jeremiah decided not to mention the LORD anymore or speak in his name, the word of the LORD is described as a burning fire in his heart and bones that he could not hold back.

Did you know? Jeremiah heard people around him crying, “Terror on Every Side,” and he described how those close to him and his enemies were looking for an opportunity to make him stumble and take revenge on him.
Did you know? In the midst of his distress, Jeremiah expressed confidence that the LORD was with him like a “mighty warrior,” and that his persecutors would stumble and not prevail.

Did you know? After his words of confidence and praise, Jeremiah returned to intense lament and cursed the day of his birth; the chapter ends with painful questions about a life of toil, sorrow, and shame.
